notes: These experiments used the unchanged R10 torque controller. They are separate from the D handoff policy. Neither supplementary detector was promoted. Gains from different splits overlap and should not be added.

initial_candidate.reason: Priority preservation fails: mass-0 1.429 s no-impact false rise makes all official 0 kg/1.42 s cells indistinguishable and loses two R10-valid official detections. Two negative-normal independent impacts also add post-event false rises.

official_evaluator.note: A higher aggregate detected-cell count does not override lost protected cells or the new no-impact false alarm.

source_review_gaps: Original candidate evaluator compares only false-alarm counts, not injective event times.
Original candidate has no model shape/finite/provenance validation and no mass/COM domain abstention.
Original candidate local evaluator omits official, perturbation, and combined runtime gates.
initial_candidate.decision: Do not package or promote. A future candidate must predeclare an out-of-domain fallback/normal model including unloaded payload and remove negative-normal post-event false rises, then repeat independent gates; no threshold tuning on this matrix.

diagnosis.interpretation: The second rise is induced by a delayed second landing/support transient after the pulse, not a residual score tail and not present in either exact no-pulse twin.

channel_audit.limitation: The candidate explicitly abstains only the supplemental tangential coordinates during inferred positive support. These examples are detected after that state ends; they do not prove general tangential separation or continuous supplemental coverage.

limitations: The support-compatible coordinate removal is a supplemental-channel abstention, not a general physical separator.
The delayed support tail still re-arms the channel after the inferred support state ends.
The fixed fresh impact matrix was not opened because regression failed.
The model path is private and absolute, so this branch is research-only and non-portable.
